headline_marked: Tk 1,276 crore project to [[reform Bangladesh's banking sector]] with World Bank funding
headline: Tk 1,276 crore project to reform Bangladesh's banking sector with World Bank funding
summary: The 'Financial Sector Support Project-2' aims to modernize technology, restructure banks, and strengthen depositor protection to tackle high non-performing loans and governance gaps.
details: The Bangladesh government is launching a new project titled 'Financial Sector Support Project-2' (FSSP-2) to reform the banking sector, increase supervisory capacity, and strengthen financial sector protection.

The project's total cost is estimated at Tk 1,276 crore, with the World Bank's International Development Association (IDA) providing Tk 1,261 crore and Bangladesh Bank providing the remaining Tk 14 crore.
The project will run from July 2024 to June 2031. It aims to address long-standing issues such as high non-performing loans (NPLs), governance deficits, and weak technological capabilities.

A significant portion of the budget is allocated for ICT infrastructure development, including Tk 711 crore for ICT equipment and Tk 355 crore for computer software to modernize the central bank's monitoring systems.

The project will be implemented in three phases: improving supervisory capacity and ICT infrastructure, strengthening financial protection and bank restructuring, and providing administrative and technical assistance.

Key goals include strengthening the Deposit Insurance Trust Fund (DITF) to better protect depositors and reducing the time required to return funds to depositors during bank liquidation or restructuring.
The initiative also focuses on improving the governance and financial stability of state-owned banks through performance-based conditions (PBCs) for reforms.
Additionally, the project includes a budget of Tk 70 crore for training 3,565 officials to enhance institutional capacity and institutional consultancy services.
caption:

headline_marked: Roof blown off in [[cocktail explosions at a house]] in Chapainawabganj
headline: Roof blown off in cocktail explosions at a house in Chapainawabganj
summary: Police and BGB are investigating a house in a remote riverine area of the Padma River after stored cocktails exploded, causing significant damage.
details: A series of cocktail explosions destroyed the tin roof of a house in Naroshia village, Jahurpur Union of Chapainawabganj Sadar upazila.
Local residents claim that the explosions occurred due to cocktails that had been stockpiled inside the house.
The blasts took place at night in the home of a local youth, causing extensive damage to the structure. No casualties have been reported.
Police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel visited the scene immediately after receiving news of the incident.
Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Chapainawabganj Sadar Model Police Station, Ekramul Hossain, stated that an investigation is underway to determine how the cocktails arrived there and who is involved.
Lt. Colonel Mustafizur Rahman, Commander of the 53 BGB, confirmed that BGB members are currently deployed at the site to maintain order.
The incident occurred approximately 3 kilometers from the Jahurpur BGB camp, and authorities report that the situation in the area is currently normal.
